findings.how_to_check: In Stata on one state's target records (e.g. `ri`), compare `sum img_n` (record-weighted) with `bysort filename: gen byte _tag = (_n==1) if filename!=""` followed by `sum img_n if _tag` (per image).
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel line 118 to reflect the record-level unit of analysis (e.g., `local r "| Mean target records on record's image |"`), or, if a true per-image mean is desired, collapse/tag unique `(st, filename)` images before summarizing `img_n`.
findings.title: "Mean target records per image" averages image size across target records rather than across images
findings.what_the_code_does: Line 39 computes `bysort filename: gen long img_n = _N` on the target-record dataset, assigning the image's target-record count `img_n` to every target record on that image. Lines 118–122 then output a row labelled `"| Mean target records per image |"` using `quietly sum img_n if ftype==`t'`. Because observations are target records rather than distinct images, an image with `k` records in column `t` is weighted `k` times (`sum_j (n_{j,t} * n_j) / sum_j n_{j,t}`), rather than weighted equally per image (`sum_j n_j / J`).
findings.why_it_matters: By the inspection paradox (size-biased sampling), averaging `img_n` across records overstates the true mean number of target records per image by `Var(n_j) / mean(n_j)`. Furthermore, comparing `sum img_n if ftype==t` across failure types `t = 0..3` conflates within-image clustering of failures with image size while presenting the numbers to the reader as `"Mean target records per image"`.

findings.how_to_check: In `MATCHING/nomodel_diag.do`, run `tab ftype if missing(img_n)` (records with `filename == ""`) and `tab ftype if missing(img_fail)` (records with `filename == ""` or `img_n == 1`).
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit rows in `MATCHING/nomodel_diag.do:110-123` reporting the count (or percentage) of records in each `ftype` column with empty `filename` (`missing(img_n)`) and with non-missing `img_fail` (`!missing(img_fail)`), and guard line 115 against `r(N) == 0` (`cond(r(N)>0, strtrim(string(100*`a'/r(N), "%6.1f")), "-")`).
findings.title: nomodel_diag.do sets img_n and img_fail to missing when filename is empty but never reports empty-filename or valid-image denominators by ftype
findings.what_the_code_does: Lines 40–41 set `img_fail = .` when `img_n <= 1 | filename == ""` and `img_n = .` when `filename == ""`, and line 44 drops `filename`. While lines 85–102 print `nmiss` for every other continuous diagnostic variable (`parsing_quality`, `namefrst_ml_prob`, `namelast_ml_prob`, `non_ditto_ml_prob`, `linep`), lines 110–123 report `"Image mostly failing (%)"` over `!missing(img_fail)` and `"Mean target records per image"` over `!missing(img_n)` without reporting how many records in each `ftype` have `filename == ""` (`missing(img_n)`) or `img_n == 1` (`missing(img_fail)`).
findings.why_it_matters: `MATCHING/nomodel_diag.do` diagnoses why 9.62% of target records lack usable model output. As lines 35–36 confirm, empty `filename` rows exist in `merged_data.dta` (e.g., census records that failed to link to a model/image row). Omitting the count or share of `filename == ""` (`missing(img_n)`) and `!missing(img_fail)` by `ftype` hides a direct cause of missing model output and leaves the effective sample sizes of the last two rows of the main table undisclosed.

findings.suggested_fix: In `MATCHING/nomodel_diag.do:135-142`, check `capture confirm string variable `v'` before the inner loop and use `` `v' == `"`val'"' `` when `_rc == 0` (or `missing(`v')` when `val == "."`). For `img_fail` at lines 38–40, consider verifying or reporting whether duplicate `(filename, linep)` rows exist among target records with `filename != ""`.
findings.title: Leave-one-out image failure counts duplicate merged_data rows as distinct neighbours, and levelsof tabulation assumes non_ditto_ml is numeric
findings.what_the_code_does: First, lines 38–40 compute `bysort filename: egen long img_nf = total(fail)` and `img_n = _N` across all rows passing line 30 without checking for duplicate `(filename, linep)` or `histid` rows, which `MATCHING/1_divide_and_clean_everyoneV5_women_addedV2.do:112-117`, `MATCHING/fs_cells.do:89-95`, and `MATCHING/profile_names_build.do:68-76` show exist in `merged_data.dta`. Any duplicated target record on the same `filename` is counted as an "'other' target record on the same image" in `(img_nf - fail)/(img_n - 1)`. Second, lines 130–142 run `quietly levelsof `v', missing local(vals)` and `quietly count if ftype==`t' & `v'==`val'` for `non_ditto` and `non_ditto_ml`; if `non_ditto_ml` is stored as a string in any state file, unquoted `` `v'==`val' `` raises `r(109)`/`r(111)`/`r(198)`.
findings.why_it_matters: Duplicate rows on the same `filename` artificially inflate `img_fail` (giving a duplicated record `img_fail = 1` if it failed or `0` if it succeeded, even if no other distinct target record exists on that image), and an unquoted `levelsof` comparison will abort the script after all 49 states have been loaded if `non_ditto_ml` is string-typed.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied for this review run, so claims-vs-code could only be evaluated against in-repo comments, generated markdown/LaTeX headers, and committed replication result files (`replication/results/*.tex`, `MATCHING/results/*.md`), not against manuscript prose.

External datasets (`$REP_SNU/.../merged_data.dta` and `$REP_F/.../profile_names.dta`) reside outside the repository and the Stata pipeline was not executed during this review, so variable storage types across all 49 state `merged_data.dta` files and exact counts of `filename == ""` or duplicate `(filename, linep)` rows are inferred from source code and logs.
structured_output.summary: The working tree contains a staged diagnostic script (`MATCHING/nomodel_diag.do`), a mid-run truncated tracked output file (`MATCHING/results/profile_names_jw.md`), two leftover `Run-Stata.ps1` wrapper scripts (`MATCHING/_run_profile_names_jw.do` and `MATCHING/_run_tgt_fallback_diag.do`), and revision notes (`review/revision-notes-2026-11-13.md`). The most urgent issue is that `MATCHING/results/profile_names_jw.md` is currently truncated mid-number at line 49 (deleting two full tables and part of a third while a background Stata job holds the file open), so committing the working tree as-is would corrupt a tracked results file. In `MATCHING/nomodel_diag.do`, the universe and 4-way failure partition reconcile exactly with `compute_model_agreement_on_discordant.tex`, but `"Mean target records per image"` actually computes a record-weighted mean of image size rather than a per-image mean, and the table drops `filename` after setting `img_n` and `img_fail` to missing on empty `filename` without reporting how many records in each failure category lack a `filename` or are excluded from the image-clustering rows.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
